core_obligations: Choose finitely many algebra generators x_i of S over R and finitely many module generators y_j of S over T, and record the two finite families of structure constants in T (proof lines 12522-12526).

Let T' be the R-subalgebra generated by those constants, which is finitely generated over R and hence Noetherian, and build the quotient algebra S' presenting the multiplication among the Y_i (proof lines 12526-12533).
Use the surjection from S' onto S, which is finite over T', to conclude that T is finite over T' and therefore of finite type over R (proof lines 12534-12539).
proof_roadmap: Collect the structure constants into a finitely generated subalgebra T' (proof lines 12521-12528).
Present S as a finite quotient of a finite algebra over T' and transfer finiteness (proof lines 12528-12540).
difficulty_reason: The Artin-Tate lemma states that if R is Noetherian, S is a finitely generated R-algebra and T is an R-subalgebra over which S is finite, then T is of finite type over R (statement lines 12513-12519). The proof does not use determinants or integrality of the generators: it writes down the two finite generating sets, collects the finitely many structure constants into a subalgebra T', presents an auxiliary algebra S' over T' with those constants as relations, and uses the resulting surjection onto S together with Noetherianity of T' to conclude that T is finite over T' (proof lines 12521-12540). The construction of S' so that it is visibly finite over T' is the substance of the argument. H2.
